generator_assessments.assessment: The presence of atypical lymphocytes in the bone marrow and the inverted CD8:CD4 ratio are consistent with Sézary syndrome.

raw_support_spans.text: Lymphocytes positive for CD3, inverted CD8:CD4 ratio, predominantly α/β positive
Flow cytometry of bone marrow: Revealed lymphocytes with atypical CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype (2% of total cells)

generator_assessments.assessment: Pink-purple dermal papules on the trunk and extremities, with preference for the extensor surfaces of the arms and legs
The clinical presentation of pink-purple dermal papules and the immunophenotypic findings of a low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal are consistent with mycosis fungoides.

raw_support_spans.text: Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)

generator_assessments.assessment: The presence of atypical lymphocytes, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements support the diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

raw_support_spans.text: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)
Admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes
T-cell receptor PCR: Matching clonal rearrangements identified in 3 skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample

response.rationale: The presence of atypical lymphocytes, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and clonal T-cell receptor rearrangements support the diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, which is a broader category that includes mycosis fungoides.

rejected.why: Sézary syndrome is a specific type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, but the provided information does not specifically support this diagnosis over other types of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
